page: Microsoft Azure E64-32as_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. Driven by an AMD EPYC 9V45 x86_64 processor clocked at 4.5 GHz, the instance allocates 32 dedicated virtual CPUs across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The memory configuration delivers 512.0 GB of system RAM, yielding a high ratio of 16.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware features include support for advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, AVX-VNNI, and cryptographic accelerators including AES and SHA-NI. The instance contains no bundled local storage, requiring attached network storage volumes, and lacks discrete GPU acceleration.

Benchmark evaluations demonstrate top-tier single-core throughput, with stress-ng single-core scores exceeding the 90th percentile and single-threaded gzip compression reaching 41.32 GB/sec. PassMark CPU and memory evaluations place the system in the top 25 percent of tested servers. Multi-core compute performance and large-block uncached memory bandwidth measuring 100.91 GB/sec read and 67.8 GB/sec write place within average ranges. In application-level benchmarks, the server processes 53.33 million Redis SET operations per second and shows top-tier throughput for small 135M-parameter language model text generation, though throughput falls significantly on larger 70B models.

The constrained-core architecture of the E64-32as_v7 provides a qualitative cost efficiency advantage for software packages licensed on a per-core basis, such as commercial relational database management systems. Deployments obtain the expansive 512 GB memory pool of a 64-vCPU chassis without incurring licensing costs for unneeded processing cores. A notable tradeoff is the absence of local ephemeral storage, making I/O performance dependent on remote Premium Storage attachments. This profile is engineered for memory-bound workloads including large in-memory databases, high-capacity Redis caches, and enterprise data processing pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure E64-32as_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine designed for memory-intensive workloads requiring high memory-to-core ratios. Powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9V45 processor operating at up to 4.5 GHz, the instance provides 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores alongside 512 GB of RAM, yielding 16 GB of memory per vCPU. The server includes no bundled local storage and no GPU accelerators, relying on network-attached Premium Storage for persistent data. Benchmark results highlight top-tier single-core compute performance and strong PassMark evaluation results, supported by AVX-512 vector extensions. Memory bandwidth and multi-core processing align with median benchmark brackets, while single-threaded compression tests place in the top decile. This configuration delivers cost efficiency for software licensed on a per-core basis that requires massive RAM capacity, making it a strong fit for large enterprise relational databases, in-memory caching tiers, Redis deployments, and memory-bound analytics.
